newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- June retail sales to set tone.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- June retail sales to set tone.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income markets, on the lookout for any rebound in consumer spending, could get their direction for the week from the release of retail sales data on Tuesday, analysts said.
Past reports of heady consumer confidence levels indicate at least some rebound in retail sales data for June, they said. A gain would follow three consecutive monthly declines in retail sales.

"Retail sales will seal the market's fate for the day and probably for the next couple of days going forward, said Anthony Karydakis, senior financial economist at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc. "That is particularly true if we have any surprises in either direction."

Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that retail sales rose 0.2 percent in June after slipping 0.1 percent in May and that sales excluding auto transactions rose 0.5 percent after falling 0.1 percent in May.
The data will be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

Don Fine, chief market analyst at Chase Asset Management, noted the past declines in retail sales "do not quite fit" given the heady measures of consumer sentiment seen from the Conference Board and the University of Michigan. Still, strong sentiment does not necessarily equal steamy sales down the road, he said.

"(High consumer confidence) does not mean one should expect retail sales to pick up and boom ahead, but does say that the three succesive declines we've seen are probably an aberration on the low side."

Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, also underscored the importance of the retail sales data to the direction of bond markets and that a break from predictions could easily move the market.

"Anything in excess of 0.5 percent (ex-autos) would probably be a problem because it would suggest there is some momentum going into the third quarter, even though it's a second quarter number," Schaja said.
Karydakis said an overall gain above 0.3 percent or 0.5 percent to 0.6 percent ex-autos would be "a little unpleasant" and may be an excuse for the market to pull back from highs.
At the same time, another decline could provide the market with enough impetus to push the long bond through the 6.50 percent level, he added.
In late trading on Monday, the benckmark bond was yielding 6.55 percent. Substantial revisions to May's data are also a distinct possibility, he said.

To a lesser extent, market participants will peer at the BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT and the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail sales index at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT.
"In June, Redbook showed a pretty solid gain of 1.7 percent so it will be interesting to see whether that strength we saw in department stores sales in June will be sustained," Karydakis said.
But the market will likely turn its focus to Wednesday's 0830 EDT/1230 GMT release of the U.S. Consumer Price Index after the release of the retail sales data, dealers said.
Dealers indicated that Federal funds would open between 5-9/16 percent and 5-5/8 percent on Tuesday.
